name: Setup and host integration
summary: Installing Open Second Brain, connecting agent hosts, the MCP server and its access, and install health.

features.name: Guided setup
features.summary: Configures the machine and the brain, connects one agent host and verifies it; a first-run checklist shows what is left.
capabilities: `o2b setup --target <host>` prints the machine, host and verify plan; nothing is written without `--apply`
`--apply` asks y/N on a terminal and refuses without `--yes` when stdin is not a TTY
Apply runs `o2b init`, writes the host registration through its install adapter and verifies it
Apply ends with an in-process MCP probe and a store self-test on throwaway storage
`o2b init` saves vault, agent name and IANA timezone to the machine config, then creates and binds the store
`o2b init --interactive` (or `setup` on a TTY without `--target`) runs a wizard that finds `.obsidian` vaults
`o2b onboarding` derives a read-only next-step checklist (store, index, identity, first signal) with commands
`o2b brain init` creates the store; on a legacy vault it scaffolds `Brain/` with `_brain.yaml` and `_BRAIN.md`
limits: Plugin hosts (Claude Code, Hermes, OpenClaw, ZCode) and `generic` get a printed manual step; setup exits 7
Setup refuses to change a configured vault, agent name or timezone; `o2b init` changes them
The Aider target requires `--vault`, because Aider reads its context from a file in the vault

features.name: Agent host installation
features.summary: Writes, checks, updates and removes the integration for each supported agent host; Aider runs inside a memory wrapper.
capabilities: Ten host adapters write the integration by JSON merge, fenced block, host CLI call, file copy or symlink, or print it
`o2b install` detects hosts, plans with a diff, writes on `--apply`, verifies on `--check`, compares on `--friction`
Writes a fenced brain-usage block into the AGENTS.md or GEMINI.md the host reads, beside the MCP registration
Uninstall removes only paths recorded in `install.lock.json`; a hand-edited fenced block needs `--force`
`o2b update` re-applies hosts whose payload sha256 changed, e.g. by `install.tool_profile`, then migrates the store
`aider wrap` passes a live context sidecar via `--read`, then saves the new chat-history tail as a capture
`brain mcp-landscape` lists MCP servers declared in vault config files: packages and env names, never values
Reports linked projects or each host's verify state (`second_brain_wiring`)
limits: Claude Code, Hermes, OpenClaw and ZCode install through their own plugin systems, not `o2b install`

features.name: Hermes memory provider
features.summary: Runs Open Second Brain as the Hermes Agent memory provider and stores Hermes built-in memory writes in the brain.
capabilities: Registers a Hermes memory provider and health check, backed by a long-lived `o2b mcp --harness hermes` child
Exposes 11 curated memory tools with live `tools/list` schemas, falling back to vendored static schemas
Fills the system prompt block with the active-preferences body from `brain_context`
Prefetch runs the recall gate, then a ranked `brain_context_pack` (1024 tokens max) and the identity reminder
Buffers each turn on a background thread and a JSONL transcript; flushes at compaction, session end and shutdown
Stores built-in memory writes (`add`/`replace` on `memory` or `user`) as `host_memory_write` continuity records
On a multiplexed gateway resolves settings from the bound Hermes profile, never the process environment
Re-renders mirrored host memory writes as unconfirmed rules after a dry run (`brain continuity promote`)
limits: Reports itself unavailable until a vault path is configured
Hermes filters out `remove` memory writes before the hook, so deletions are not mirrored
A failed bridge call injects nothing for that turn; there is no second recall lane

features.name: OpenClaw native plugin
features.summary: A native OpenClaw plugin with status, page listing and health tools and a per-turn agent identity reminder.
capabilities: Registers `second_brain_status`, `second_brain_query` and `vault_health` in-process and spawns no subprocess
Prepends the identity reminder per model call via `before_prompt_build` `prependContext`, not the cached prompt
Names the agent by a host-qualified identity derived from vendor `openclaw` and the operator name
`second_brain_query` lists vault pages by case-insensitive title substring, limit 1 to 500 (default 50)
Serves at remote reach: pages reserved against remote reads and quarantined entity pages are withheld
Status redacts config values, including secrets resolved from the custody store
Resolves the vault from plugin config `vault`, then `VAULT_DIR`, then the working directory
limits: Read-only: memory writes go through the separately registered MCP server
Exposes three tools, not the MCP tool surface

features.name: MCP server and tool profiles
features.summary: Serves the tools over stdio or HTTP, with tool profiles and a two-pass catalog for hosts with tool limits.
capabilities: Serves MCP over stdio by default or Streamable HTTP on 127.0.0.1 with a Host/Origin DNS-rebinding guard
Refuses to serve HTTP beyond loopback without `--api-key` or a minted token
Tool profiles full, writer (5 always-loaded tools), catalog, recall, minimal; an unknown profile exits 2
Returns the compact tool catalog or the full schemas of named tools (`tool_hydrate`)
Narrows the served tools with `--allow-tool`, `--disable-tool` and `--max-tools`
Results over 2000 characters are parked, redacted, for 24 h as artifacts; `brain_artifact_get` returns them
Summarizes per-tool call latency at p50, p95 and p99 once `mcp_route_metrics_enabled` records it
Runs a tool handler from the shell (`o2b tool-call <tool> --tool-arg k=v`)
limits: HTTP answers each request with one JSON or single-event SSE response; progress tokens are refused there
A server with no vault starts, but tools that need vault files refuse with `vault_required`
Route metrics store tool, scope, status, duration and argument names, never argument values

features.name: Per-agent MCP tokens
features.summary: Named per-agent tokens for the HTTP transport, and one-command provisioning of a host with its token.
capabilities: `mcp token mint --agent` creates `mcp_token_<slug>` from 32 random bytes and prints the material exactly once
Stores only the sha256 hash and a 12-character prefix in `mcp-tokens.json`, mode 0600 or an owner-only ACL
An HTTP request whose bearer or `X-API-Key` matches a token runs as that token's agent for that request
Keeps the old material valid for 10 minutes after `rotate`, with no restart
`mcp_tokens_required` (default off) refuses credential-less HTTP requests once any token exists
Every mint, rotation and revocation appends a value-free record to the secret-custody audit
`o2b bootstrap --target` registers the host, mints its token and writes `bootstrap.lock.json`; reruns are no-ops
Tears a provision down with `bootstrap --remove`: uninstalls, revokes the token, drops the receipt
limits: Tokens authenticate only the HTTP transport; a stdio registration keeps its config-derived identity
A token sets identity only; tool profiles and reach still bind every caller
Bootstrap covers codex, grok, opencode (adapter), generic (print), claude-code and zcode (verify only)

features.name: Install health checks
features.summary: Reports configuration, vault and plugin health, the installed version and a redacted config snapshot.
capabilities: `o2b status` prints config path, config keys, a semantic-search hint and the brain store state, also as JSON
`o2b doctor` checks vault and config writability, plugin manifests, Hermes resolver parity and codegraph
Prints a fix command for each failed doctor check
`doctor --readiness` probes model key, embeddings, adapters, installed hosts and write-back, 5 s timeout each
`doctor selftest` opens, indexes, writes, searches and deletes on a throwaway vault and store
`second_brain_status` returns redacted config, vault, Brain, search index, vault-scope and store blocks
`vault_health` adds runtime notices and a state-surface inventory (path, reachability, override) to the checks
Writes a redacted config snapshot through the egress guard (`export-config`)
limits: Plain `o2b doctor` refuses without a configured vault; `doctor selftest` needs none
Readiness probes run only with `--readiness`; a probe that times out reports unknown, not failed
